name: Slyth
body:
Slyths are one of the oldest races. When the planet was newly born, slyths populated miles and miles of uninterrupted caverns deep below the surface. Then came a great cataclysm. Tectonic plates shifted and collided all across the globe, causing tsunamis, flooding, cave-ins, and drastic geographical changes. So few slyths survived that the race was no longer a thriving population, but instead, only tiny tribal pockets remained in just a few remote mountainous regions of the world.

Physical Description

Slyths are bipedal humanoids. Small scales, much like a snake’s, cover a slyth’s head, neck, and shoulders. Indeed, their facial features bear several similarities to snakes or dragons, particularly their flat-profiled noses, high-sculpted cheekbones, and yellow-slitted pupils. A hoodlike flap of skin (like a cobra hood) covers a slyth’s head, ending at the shoulders. Once the scaled skin tapers off at the shoulders, the rest of a slyth’s body is indistinguishable from a human’s.

Every female slyth has a unique color pattern to her scales, while a male’s scales are a uniform jet black. Also unique to female slyths is a trio of bony plates on the forehead, similar to those found on a dragon’s forehead.

Both male and female slyths are hairless. They are tall with narrow hips and prominent bones. Slyths can contort their limbs into seemingly impossible angles to fit through tiny spaces and narrow tunnels.

Finally, though a slyth uses their nose to smell, they also use their long, thin, forked tongue to augment their sense of smell by poking it out of their mouth and moving it back and forth.

Society

Slyths have always passed on their knowledge, history, and traditions orally.

Their only permanent records were pictographs, chiseled or painted on cavern walls. When the interconnected cavern system was destroyed during the cataclysm, leaving only tiny pockets of surviving slyths cut off from each other and scattered, much of their history was lost. With the population decimated, the elders dead, and communication between individual communities cut off, different groups developed customs unique to their small tribes.

The origin of the slyths is one historical detail consistent among all the tribes. They claim to be the little brothers and sisters of the great wyrms. Slyths worship the good dragon deities and believe the deities created them to live as helpmates to silver and copper dragons. These dragons resided in the hills and mountains, protecting the slyths from topside threats, while the slyths kept an eye on the duergar who might wish to cause havoc with the dragons from below.

Over the centuries, these tiny familial groups have struggled to maintain a viable population. Though cautious of the topside world after having lived sheltered lives in tight-knit family groups, the slyths decided to migrate to the planet’s surface, hoping to find others of their kind with whom to grow their dwindling population. Only now are the various slyth tribes starting to reconnect. As they do so, they integrate the various tribal customs into the whole, such that their traditions continue to morph and grow as they begin anew as one people.

Relations

Slyths treat all good metallic dragons with respectful affection and consider duergar to be their enemies. Slyths value straightforwardness, honesty, and cooperation. Reading between the lines, discerning sarcasm, or deciphering the subtle nuances and undertones of verbal communication is challenging for a slyth.

Slyths are most comfortable among societies built upon equality and responsibility towards family. Feudal societies that thrive on a peasant/noble hierarchy that creates a divide between landowners and workers conflict with their sense of fairness and universal access to resources.

As a generalization, groups of traveling slyths keep to themselves, leading nomadic lives. As they migrate with the seasons, they hope to find other lost tribes. Perhaps someday, they will create a permanent settlement they can call home near a mountain range with plentiful caves, geothermal vents, and sulfuric springs.

Alignment and Religion

As members of a small population, every slyth is aware of how important each contributing individual is to the welfare of the tribal unit. Youngsters are taught from birth to view the clan’s success as their success. Slyth are fiercely protective of those they call family or friends. They are honest, transparent, and group-minded.

Their instinct to protect and nurture others leads many slyths to healing vocations.

Most slyths are good, with a preference for order over disorder. Very few slyths are evil, and those who commit serious violence against other members of the tribe get cast out for the safety of the group.

Most slyths revere the good dragon deities. Slyths believe these deities created them to be helpmates to the powerful and magnificent metallic dragons.

Adventurers

Slyths journey from place to place because they hope to locate other slyths. When a slyth gets separated from their kin or becomes the lone survivor of an attack against their clan, they may join a group of traveling individuals for protection. Slyths prefer companionship over solitude and recognize that choice rather than blood forms some families.

Male Names: Ssalvador, Ssevill, Ssorik, Ssurich, Ssval. Female Names: Essbeth, Esslynn, Essmarra, Esstrish.

Core Traits
Ability Score Modifiers: Slyths are flexible and friendly, but their centuries of living in isolation leaves them less informed. They gain +2 to Dexterity and Charisma, but suffer -2 to Intelligence
Type: Slyths are humanoids with the slyth subtype.
Size: Medium. Though on the taller end of the spectrum compared to most humans, slyths are Medium creatures and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.
Speed: Slyths have a base speed of 30 feet.
Cave Dweller: Slyths gain a +1 bonus on Knowledge (dungeoneering) and Survival checks made underground.
Contortionist: Slyths gain a +1 racial bonus on Escape Artist checks and on their CMD against grapple attempts.
Light-Footed: Slyths reduce the penalty for using Stealth while moving by 5 and can make Stealth checks while running at a -20 penalty. (This number includes the penalty reduction from this trait.)
Heat Tolerant: Slyths receive a +4 racial bonus on Constitution checks and Fortitude saves to avoid the ill effects of thirst and hot environments. Additionally, they take only half scalding damage from boiling water. Conversely, slyths take a -4 racial penalty on Fortitude saves to avoid the ill effects of cold environments.
Senses: Darkvision. Slyths can in the dark up to 120 feet. Additionally, slyths gain the scent ability.
Languages: Slyths begin play speaking Common and Draconic. Slyths with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Duergar, Dwarf, Orc, Terran, and Undercommon.
Alternate Traits

The following racial traits may be selected instead of the standard racial traits for slyth characters.

Armored Hood: The eyesight of some slyths is not as penetrating as other members of their race, but their scaled hood is thicker than usual. These slyths have a +1 natural armor bonus, but the range of their darkvision is only 60 feet. This replaces darkvision (120 feet).
Cooperative Clanmate: Some slyths are especially successful when coordinating their efforts with others. These slyths select one bonus teamwork feat of their choice at 1st level. This replaces cave dweller and light-footed.
Dragon Friend: These slyths are slightly less flexible than other slyths, but they make up for it with bravery. They gain a +4 racial bonus against a dragon’s frightful presence ability. This replaces contortionist.
Hale: Some slyths don’t have as developed a sense of smell as others. Instead, they are more resistant to poison and fire than other members of their race. These slyths gain a bonus on saving throws against poison effects equal to their Hit Dice and resistance to fire 5. This replaces scent.

Into the Wilds: Mountains and Volcanoes, Copyright 2024, Bloodstone Press; author Beth Jones
